headline: Middletown veterans cemetery expansion will add 1,510 cremation plots
dek: A $584,250 federal grant, paired with $294,250 in state money, will help Connecticut expand its only state-operated veterans cemetery as cremation burial space nears capacity.
body: Connecticut will expand the State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown with 1,510 new burial plots for cremated remains, state officials announced Friday. The project will use a $584,250 grant from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs alongside $294,250 that Connecticut has already allocated, adding capacity at a cemetery that serves veterans and eligible family members from across the state. The [governor’s announcement](https://portal.ct.gov/governor/news/press-releases/2026/10-2026/governor-lamont-announces-funding-to-expand-the-connecticut-state-veterans-cemetery-in-middletown) was also covered locally by [Middletown Patch](https://patch.com/connecticut/middletown-ct/middletown-veterans-cemetery-expansion-add-cremation-burial-plots).

The work is planned for a parcel next to the existing cemetery at 317 Bow Lane. The property was formerly used by Connecticut Valley Hospital and was recently transferred from the state Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services to the Department of Veterans Affairs, which is overseeing the expansion. The location allows the state to extend an existing cemetery rather than wait for a separate site to be developed.

Under the state’s announcement, the federal money will pay for the cremains burial plots and related site work, including an entrance gate, fencing, landscaping, irrigation components, concrete-block storage bays, site furnishings and supporting infrastructure. The state funding will support demolition of Cottage 22, a vacant Connecticut Valley Hospital building on the property. Connecticut has not announced a completion date for the construction.

The expansion is aimed at a specific capacity problem. The [Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs](https://portal.ct.gov/dva/cemetery-and-memorial-services) says the Middletown cemetery currently has 14,718 burial plots and 3,000 columbarium niches. State officials estimate that the existing supply of in-ground cremation plots will be exhausted around January 2028 without additional space; with the expansion, those plots are projected to remain available through at least December 2033.

That timing matters because the cemetery offers several distinct choices for families. The project concerns in-ground burial of cremated remains, while casket burials and above-ground columbarium niches are separate options. The state says extending the cremation-plot supply through 2033 would bring the estimated depletion dates for all three options into alignment, giving officials time to plan a future cemetery intended to serve veterans and their families over the longer term.

The Middletown site was established in 1985 and is the largest state-operated veterans cemetery in Connecticut, according to the Department of Veterans Affairs. The department’s [cemetery-services page](https://portal.ct.gov/dva/cemetery-and-memorial-services) says the site is the final resting place for more than 16,000 veterans and family members. Connecticut also maintains the Colonel Raymond F. Gates Cemetery in Rocky Hill, which is reserved primarily for veterans residing at the state’s residential and skilled-nursing facilities, and provides perpetual care for Spring Grove Veterans Cemetery in Darien, which is closed to new burials.

The funding announcement follows a longer state effort to secure land and keep the Middletown facility eligible for federal cemetery support. A [2023 state bond authorization](https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/opm/bud-capital-budget/agendas/cy-2023/agenda%5Fdec15%5F2023.pdf) set aside $3 million for land acquisition and improvements connected to the Department of Veterans Affairs cemetery program. A subsequent state planning document said the Middletown cemetery was expected to approach capacity within several years, while an [environmental scoping notice](https://portal.ct.gov/CEQ/DAS/Scoping-Notice/DVA-Cemetery-Expansion) identified the Bow Lane expansion area and estimated that existing space could be depleted in about 4.6 years.

For Connecticut veterans’ families, the immediate result is a planned increase in local burial capacity, not a new benefit or completed construction project. The state and federal awards still have to be translated into demolition, site preparation and cemetery improvements. The announcement does not specify the construction schedule or the final operating date for the new plots. The Department of Veterans Affairs will remain responsible for project oversight and for coordinating burial services while the expansion proceeds.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Middletown veterans cemetery expansion adds 1,510 plots
seoDescription: Connecticut will use federal and state funding to add 1,510 cremation burial plots at the State Veterans Cemetery in Middletown.
